| Scene description | • Observation block S01-A is in Donghu Jingyuan Residential Community, Hongshan District, in a typical residential setting.<br>• S01-A-01: a centralized disposal point beneath a sorting shelter contains several clean black other-waste bins without visible overflow, beside planting and pavement.<br>• S01-A-02: white bags, foam food containers, transparent cups, cardboard, and black waste bags form one accumulation on soil beside trees and shrubs.<br>• S01-A-03: a clean roadside stainless-steel bin with other-waste and recyclables openings is not full; a white vehicle is behind it.<br>• S01-A-04: a green mesh bag containing corn husks and other food waste stands beside a tree at the path edge, without overflowing.<br>• S01-A-05: two green bins and one black bin at the market entrance all overflow with plastic bags, foam netting, and leaves. | Severity | **Severe.** Five overflowing bins and one obvious accumulation are reported. Waste on soil within planting may cause secondary pollution and vector breeding; overflow and scattered waste at the market entrance impair residential conditions and appearance, indicating management failures. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: waste scattered in planting causes visual pollution and may breed insects and rodents and transmit pathogens; market entrance overflow and ground litter affect pedestrian access and sanitation. Possible short-term impacts: delayed removal may allow wind dispersal, rain-induced wastewater leakage, soil and groundwater pollution, and increased complaints, damaging the community's governance image. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** too few containers or delayed collection. All three market bins at S01-A-05 overflow near fruit stalls, suggesting collection turnover may not match high generation. Compare collection frequency with waste quantities.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** weak sorting awareness or poorly placed disposal points. Mixed waste at S01-A-02 lies beside shrubs at an undesignated location, possibly from residents. Check disposal guidance and surveillance records.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** inadequate inspections and maintenance. Overflow and litter at S01-A-05 show no prompt cleaning, suggesting absent or ineffective inspections. Review inspection records and collection logs. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, the problem may undermine trust in waste sorting and worsen disposal behavior; create vector breeding sites and public health risks; expose managers to repeated penalties affecting operating qualifications and reputation; and lead to designation as a priority supervision area, increasing management costs and enforcement pressure. |
| Recommendations | **Immediate actions:** remove waste at S01-A-02; empty overflowing market bins at S01-A-05 and provide spare bins or more collections; inspect all disposal points, record overflow, and arrange urgent removal; install warnings or temporary barriers around accumulations.<br>**Long-term measures:** adjust container provision to waste generation, particularly near markets; strengthen sorting awareness through notices, boards, and WeChat groups; establish daily inspections and removal with named responsible organizations and personnel linked to assessments; install monitoring at priority locations, including markets and sorting shelters, to trace violations. |
| Priority | **High.** Obvious accumulation and multiple overflowing bins cause visual pollution and potential sanitation risks at residential and market access areas. Broad exposure and public concern require immediate action to prevent escalation. |
